newsitem.title: UK: IRA suspect killed as police foil major UK attack.
newsitem.headline: IRA suspect killed as police foil major UK attack.

text.p: An Irish guerrilla suspect was killed on Monday during police raids said to have foiled an imminent IRA bomb attack in Britain.
The dead man was wounded in a shoot-out as police officers arrested him and five other suspects. Police said he died in hospital shortly afterwards.
There were no immediate details of the shooting incident or the identity of the dead man but it was certain to inflame the fragile peace process in Northern Ireland.
Police said they had recovered a "very large" quantity of explosives as well as firearms and bomb-making equipment.

"The operation has undoubtedly frustrated a serious imminent IRA (Irish Republican Army) terrorist attack on the British mainland involving the deployment of a large vehicle bomb likely to have caused grave loss of life and massive disruption," police said in a statement.
The IRA has planted a number of bombs in Britain since calling off a 17-month long ceasefire in February, citing British intransigence over the progress of peace efforts in Northern Ireland.
British and Irish security sources had speculated last week that the guerrillas might be preparing to call a new ceasefire in their 25-year-long campaign to end British rule of Northern Ireland.
The IRA's political wing Sinn Fein has denied the reports and Monday's police swoop suggested that the guerrillas were in fact planning another large bomb attack.
Sinn Fein has been excluded from all-party peace talks that started in Belfast in June on a political settlement for Northern Ireland because of the IRA's refusal to reinstate its ceasefire.
Chief Sinn Fein strategist Martin McGuiness said on Saturday the talks should be scrapped because they were going nowhere.

The last IRA attacks were in June when a truck bomb exploded in the middle of the northern English city of Manchester, injuring more than 200 people. Two weeks later IRA guerrillas fired mortars at a British army base in Germany. There were no injuries.

Monday's police swoop was the third major setback for the IRA this year. In February an IRA guerrilla blew himself up with his own bomb on a London bus and police later found a bomb factory at his London home.

In July, British police arrested eight people and recovered bomb-making equipment sufficient for 36 bombs which they believe would have been used to target gas, water and electricity installations in London.
